#### 🧠 How I work

- **Correct first, then fast.** Locks, retries and recovery jobs before any cache.
- **Boring to run.** Health checks, alerts and zero-downtime deploys are part of the feature.
- **Tests are the spec.** Unit, integration and end-to-end, written with the code.
- **Own it end to end.** Scope, design, ship, then watch it in production.
- **Leave people better.** Reviews that teach, and docs the next dev can follow.

## 🏗️ Architecture Spotlight: Ynmo Pay

One payment service in front of every app: card payments, BNPL and bank payroll go out, signed webhooks come back through a locked queue, and every transaction is mirrored to the accounting platform.

<p align="center">
  <img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mario237/mario237/main/assets/architecture.svg" width="100%" alt="Web, mobile and admin apps call the Laravel payment service, which talks to MyFatoorah, Tabby and STC Bank; webhooks go through a Redis queue to a two-way Qoyod accounting sync; deployed with Bitbucket CI to Docker Swarm on Google Cloud" />
</p>

<details>
<summary><b>What made it hard, and how it was solved</b></summary>
<br />

| Problem | Solution |
| --- | --- |
| Payment providers call back asynchronously | Secure webhook endpoints feeding a queue, with end-to-end reconciliation |
| Two-way accounting sync created duplicate customers | Customer deduplication and race-condition-safe upserts via unique locks, plus recovery jobs |
| Enterprise bank payroll API | OAuth2 over mutual TLS (mTLS) |
| Failures must never go unnoticed | Docker Swarm on GCP through Bitbucket CI/CD, with Slack and email error alerting |

</details>
